correctness.rationale: The complete proof isolates every pair of coordinates in the generated cyclic subgroup by intersections of two different named relation-lines, proves the proposed classes have identical separately labelled row/column/symbol neighbour-count vectors and are all separated, then derives every automorphism as (x,y)->(tx+a,ty+b) and computes its two-point stabilizer t≡1 mod h. Explicit congruence obstructions prove exact orbit failure outside generator and (n,h)=(4,2) cases. Independent scripts check exact partitions for 231 pairs n<=22, quotient vectors and all modular-unit orbits for 190 pairs n<=20, and exhaustive small-order autotopism triples n<=5. Finite tests do not establish the general quantifiers.

value.rationale: The natural question is whether local, finite-variable relational counting symmetry matches actual pointwise-autotopism orbits after two marked cells. The theorem gives an exact all-parameter subgroup-coordinate refinement partition and a sharp, unexpected orbit-exactness dichotomy. It makes substantive structural distinctions between cyclic and elementary abelian binary Latin tables, rather than only computing a small exceptional graph or an arbitrary parameter slice.
